title: How many buses does the school trip need this year?
description: Three full buses carried one hundred sixty two people last year, and this year two hundred four students go. The video finds how many people each bus holds, how many buses are needed, and whether all of them will be full.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a count must be whole, a fraction of a bus is rounded up to the next whole bus. Watch for students who round three point seven eight down to three buses, which would leave some students behind.

video_script.why: Buses and people stay in proportion, but a count of buses is a whole number, so the answer from the proportion must be rounded up.
video_script.substitution: Find how many people one bus holds, divide the new number of people by it, and round up to a whole bus.
video_script.anchor: the school trip buses from the book, three full last year and a bigger group this year

final_answer.value: 4 buses; they will not all be full (12 seats empty)
final_answer.spoken: four buses, and they will not all be full because twelve seats stay empty

never_show: 3 buses marked as enough for 204 students
maths_rules: buses needed: 204 ÷ 54 = 3.78 (about), more than 3, so round up to 4
video_script.design: One idea: a bus cannot be split, so the buses from the proportion are rounded up. The buses stay in a row on the stage and the working shows the capacity and the seats.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many buses will be needed, and will all of them be full?

beats.on_screen: Given: 3 full buses carried 162 people; 204 students this year

marks.given: the buses, the people and the new number of students are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three full buses carried one hundred sixty two people. This year there are two hundred four students.

beats.on_screen: To find: the buses needed, and whether all are full

marks.find: the two things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number of buses, and check if all of them are full.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Step one, find the people in one bus. One hundred sixty two divided by three is fifty four.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Step two, divide the students by the people in one bus. Two hundred four divided by fifty four is about three point seven eight.
<bookmark mark='more'/>That is more than three buses.

beats.on_screen: 3 buses hold 3 × 54 = 162, less than 204; so round up to 4

marks.three: 3 × 54 = 162 is written and marked too small

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, three buses hold only one hundred sixty two people, which is too few.
<bookmark mark='up'/>We round up to the next whole number, which is four.
<bookmark mark='cap'/>Step four, four buses can carry four times fifty four, which is two hundred sixteen people.
<bookmark mark='left'/>That is twelve more than two hundred four.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check. Two hundred four students and twelve empty places fill two hundred sixteen places exactly.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 4 buses; they will not all be full (12 seats empty)

marks.ans: the answer is boxed and twelve seats on the last bus are shaded empty

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The school needs four buses.
They will not all be full, because twelve seats stay empty.
